body.x: Brava, a food-tech company for home, introduced its upgraded version of the smart oven named Brava Glass at CES 2023 in the food tech section at The Venetian Expo. After the brand's launch and the first commercial product in 2018, Brava added a 97% tint glass window on the front of its original light-powered oven to fulfill the demand from its customers. Brava hopes users to observe the cooking experience in real-time - through the new transparent view of the appliance's interior and lamps in cooking action.

Brava Glass also strengthened Brava's Pure Light Cooking™ technology while keeping cooking capacities and modes as its predecessor - including Air-Fry, Roast, Bake, Sear, Toast, Reheat, Rice Cook, Slow Cook, Dehydrate and Keep Warm. Further, this updated iteration maintained the heat-resistant internal camera and machine vision to monitor cooking with a remote view possible through the Brava Home smartphone app. The oven also equips advanced sensors like a temperature probe for accurate and consistent cooks.

body.cap: Overview of Brava's booth in The Venetian Expo | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Brava stated that it remains committed to all home cookers aspiring for better food at home with its new tech product. "Since introducing Brava to the world in 2018, we've been overwhelmed with the positive response as Brava continues to make a lasting impact on daily cooking habits and kitchens across America," said John Pleasants, Co-Founder, and CEO of Brava. "With the addition of Brava Glass to our product lineup, we hope to bring an even more immersive cooking experience to families that mimics the shared nostalgia of cooking around a grill, stovetop, or campfire."

Brava continued that Glass can cook meals with less energy than it takes to a traditional oven at accurate temperatures through its multi-zone capabilities. It then highlighted the oven's ability to cook meat, veggies, and starch all on one tray — helping home chefs to reduce stress from multitasking and make a quality meal at home.

body.cap: The control panel on the top of Brava Glass | Photo by AVING News

body.x: "When we created Brava, while we went through several prototypes before landing on a final design that captured the look and function we dreamed of, we always envisioned a glass window," said Thomas Cheng, Co-Founder, and CTO of Brava. "With Brava Glass, our inspiration has come full circle as we continue to prioritize user experiences, giving cooks at every level more control and the opportunity to witness our innovative technology in action."

Brava anticipates the Glass oven will ship in early 2023, available at $1995.00. Brava Glass will include the Chef's Choice set consisting of two glass trays, two metal trays, a muffin tin, a square pan, a loaf pan, an egg tray, and the cast iron chef's pan.
